label: ככ and ככרין: talents, or silver karsh?

readings.meaning: talents: ככ and ככרין look interchangeable

note: The scroll writes the unit in full (ככרין) in some entries and as ככ in others. If ככ means talents, as the text shown here takes it, the sums are very large. If it means karsh, 300 karsh make one talent, and about 30 sums become some 300 times smaller. Høgenhaven points out that IV 12 ('silver, ככ seventy') matches II 6 ('silver, ככרין seventy'), and that XII 1 has 'gold, ככ', which a karsh of silver cannot be. Lefkovits points out that later hands corrected only some ככ to ככרין. The research files leave the question open. The translation says “talents” for both spellings.

label: כלי דמע: vessels of offering
note: In Exodus 22:28 and in the Mishnah, דמע is produce set apart as an offering for the priests. The scroll pairs it with “vessels” in many entries. The translation says “vessels of offering”; the phrase can also mean vessels that held such offerings.

label: וכתבן אצלם: “their record beside them”?

readings.meaning: at a given distance beside them

note: The phrase recurs at V 7 and XI 1, 4, 11 and 15. Milik, followed by Pixner, García Martínez, Vermes and Lange, makes it begin the next item; Puech and Lefkovits make it end the entry. Puech's text, as the research files quote it, has ב where the text shown has כ. Read with כ, it says that a written record lies with the deposit, which is how Pfann takes it. The translation follows the text shown. The research files leave the meaning open (Q5).

label: בחרובא: the ruin (Ḥorebbeh)

readings.meaning: 'little ruin'; Ḥorebbeh = monastery of Chorembe, near Kh. el-Mafjar
'little ruin'; name survives as the monastery of Chorembe
form with waw (gloss not given in the files)
form with waw (gloss not given in the files)

note: Milik and Puech read a yod ('little ruin') and take it as the place Ḥorebbeh, later the monastery of Chorembe; Lefkovits, Lurie and Muchowski read a waw, and the text shown (חרובא) also has a waw. No published report describes a ruin with steps that fits, so the research files keep this entry at the level of the valley.

label: שבעמק עכור: the Valley of Achor

readings.meaning: Valley of Achor = Wadi Nuweiʿimeh, NE of Jericho (late tradition)
Wadi Nuweiʿimeh, NE of Jericho; rejects the Buqeia

note: Reading עבור 'go past' would remove the valley altogether. Among those who read Achor, Milik and Puech follow the late tradition (Eusebius: 'north of Jericho', near Galgala) and place it in Wadi Nuweiʿimeh, while Allegro and Eshel prefer the Buqeia, the Iron Age valley; the research files rate Wadi Nuweiʿimeh best-supported but low for this entry and leave the choice open.

label: אמות {ארוה} ארבעין: the distance in cubits
note: The word after 'cubits' is disputed: Puech reads a unit word, Lefkovits reads 'one', which makes the distance 41 cubits instead of 40, and Milik deletes it. The text shown marks the letters ארוה as cancelled, as Milik does; Lefkovits also reports Wolters's reading of I 2–3 in two different ways (p. 36 against p. 41 n. 58), and the files give no preference.

label: שדת: a chest or a carrying chair
note: The letters agree; the editors disagree on what kind of container held the silver. The files record both glosses and do not choose.

label: ΚΕΝ: Greek letters

readings.meaning: Greek letters closing the entry; perhaps an abbreviated name
perhaps an abbreviated name; gap of 2–3 letters before it

note: All editions read the same letters, which follow 'seventeen talents'. As a Greek numeral ΚΕΝ would be 75, and the research files rule out the numeral idea; the personal-name idea stays open, and ΚΕΝ is the one group whose match with a name in Josephus carries some weight.

label: בנפש: the funerary monument

readings.meaning: grouped with entry 1 at Ḥorebbeh, Valley of Achor

note: The meaning 'funerary monument' is secure, but where it stood is not. Puech groups this entry with entry 1 in the Valley of Achor, the research files also keep the Kidron tomb monuments in Jerusalem as a possible place, and no individual monument has been identified.

label: בנדבך השלשי: the third course
note: The lexicon rates the meaning of נדבך as medium; it occurs once in the Bible (Ezra 6:4) and in the Mishnah (for example m. Middot 3:7). The files record no editor who reads it differently.

label: שבחצר הפרסטלין: the court of the peristyle

readings.meaning: Temple area: 'little peristyle', popular name of the inner court's wall
perhaps with entry 1 at Ḥorebbeh, Valley of Achor (queried)

note: The Greek loanword 'peristyle' is secure, the only secure landmark word in the files' Jerusalem block of entries. Milik puts the court in the Temple; Puech's overview places entry 3, with a question mark, in the Valley of Achor, and the research files keep both areas as possible.

label: סתום בחליא: closed … (sense unclear)
note: The editions agree on the letters but not on the sense. Puech's 2002 paper rendered I 7 with 'sediment', which his 2006 edition does not keep, and the files list חליא among landmark words that still have no lexicon entry.

label: בתל: the mound

readings.meaning: a tell (mound), one of the features Koḥlit needs

note: The lexicon rates the meaning as medium. A mound suits Eshel's 'ruins of Koḥlit' and Puech's Tell es-Sultan, an old ruin-mound by the 1st century, but that identification is only a hypothesis.

label: כחלת: Koḥlit

readings.meaning: cannot be identified; 'located in the desert'
Tell es-Sultan, only if Achor is Wadi Nuweiʿimeh

note: The name is secure here, but no ancient text outside the scroll places Koḥlit. The research files keep Tell es-Sultan as possible, low, and set aside Milik's Carmel, Goranson's Transjordan and Zissu's Samarian desert because they break the order of the entries.

label: והאצר: the treasury
note: The lexicon rates the meaning as medium: about 41 of 70 biblical uses name a treasury or storehouse as a place. The files record no editor who reads the word differently.

label: מפוגל: 'disqualified' or 'mouth of the heap'
note: Puech reads one word, 'disqualified', which describes the tithe; Milik divides it as 'from the mouth of the heap', which adds a landmark. The text shown has Puech's letters, and the files do not choose.

label: ניקרת הטבילה: the place of immersion

readings.meaning: baths known in Hasmonaean and Herodian Jericho

note: Puech's reading makes the landmark a built bath; the others make it a cleft in the rock. The text shown has ניקרת, as Milik reads; no immersion installation is reported at Tell es-Sultan, the files do not choose, and Puech 2015 also restores a ה in a lacuna on this line.

label: ΧΑΓ: Greek letters

readings.meaning: Greek letters closing the entry; perhaps an abbreviated name

note: The letters are agreed; unusually, they follow a place description rather than an amount. Chageiras is itself a restored name in the Josephus text, and ΧΑΓ begins no proper name in Josephus, so the research files rate these identifications weak.

label: המעבא: spiral stair or foundry

readings.meaning: spiral staircase, as in 11QTemple and m. Middot 4:5

note: Puech reads samekh, a spiral staircase of the kind the Temple Scroll and the Mishnah describe; Milik read ayin, a mine (1960) or a foundry (1962). The text shown has Milik's letters; the files record both and do not choose.

label: מנס: Manos

readings.meaning: an unplaced name, 'of Manos' (meaning rated low)

note: No ancient text outside the scroll mentions a place Manos. The lexicon compares the noun מָנוֹס 'refuge' and the Mishnaic personal name מנסיא, but the files do not say which editor takes which sense.

label: המלח: the Millo, the Esplanade or salt
note: The same word recurs at III 8 and III 11, where Milik and Puech take it as the Temple Esplanade and Puech's 2002 paper had 'salt'. The files leave the meaning open and keep only the Tyropoeon valley in Jerusalem as a possible place for this entry.

label: 41: the sum in talents

readings.meaning: same as Puech (not among the six numeral differences)
same as Puech (not among his numeral differences)

note: The research files give this sum as 42 talents and list no edition that reads it differently. The numeral signs in the text shown add up to 41 (20 + 20 + 1), so the figure here differs from all three editions as the files report them.

label: ΗΝ: Greek letters

readings.meaning: gap of about 4 letters before it

note: All editions read ΗΝ. On standard values it is 58, and the research files rule out Ullendorff's numeral readings because they need at least four different rules for five groups.

label: בית המדח: the house of MDH
note: The files report the key word four ways (המדה, המרה, המדח, חמדה); the text shown has המדח. The name is not anchored in any ancient text, the lexicon rates it low, and the files keep only the Temple area as a possible setting.

label: ברובד: on the course or terrace
note: The lexicon rates the meaning as medium; its parallels are in the Mishnah (m. Middot 3:6; 4:4; m. Yoma 4:3). The files record no editor who reads the letters differently.

label: ΘΕ: Greek letters

readings.meaning: the numeral 65, the amount in the line

readings.ref: p. 345; via Puech CSS p. 81 n. 61

note: ΞΕ would equal 65, the number of gold ingots in the line, but both facsimiles show a Θ, and the research files do not let a numerical coincidence choose the reading. The Theboutis link rests on two letters that begin 43 names in Josephus, so it is weak.

label: בצריח: the underground chamber
note: The lexicon rates the meaning as medium-high. The files record no editor who reads the word differently, though the project atlas allows 'tower' as well as 'chamber'.

label: שבחצר מתיה עצין: the court of … wood

readings.meaning: engraved מ for ב: 'the court of the wood stores'
wood stores of the Temple courts (m. Middot)

note: Reading 'wood stores' needs an emendation of the engraved letters and puts the cache in a court of the Temple; reading the name Matthiyah makes it someone's court. Puech's own text and commentary disagree here; the text shown keeps the engraved מתיה, and the files do not choose.

label: השער המזרחי: the East Gate

readings.meaning: the Golden Gate, only eastern exit of the Temple enclosure
can only be the Temple's East Gate
city East Gate (Neh 3:29) or Temple Eastern Gate (m. Middot)
in the Temple area; Jerusalem is never named

note: All editions read the same words; the question is which gate. The research files follow the Temple's East Gate (best-supported, medium) and did not adopt Thiering's Qumran door.

label: אמות תשע עסרא: the distance from the gate
note: The distance from the gate differs between the two editions. The text shown reads תשע עסרא, nineteen, as Lefkovits does, not Puech's fifteen; the files give no preference.

label: ובמזקא: and in the channel

readings.who: Pixner; Wolters; García Martínez; Vermes; Wise

note: The lexicon rates 'channel' as medium, and Allegro and Luria read other letters. Milik and several others make the channel a separate hiding place from the cistern, while Puech and Lefkovits keep one entry; the files leave that open.

label: ΔΙ: Greek letters
note: All editions read ΔΙ, which stands where the editors disagree about whether a new hiding place begins. As a numeral it would be 14, not the ten talents of the line, and the research files reject Ullendorff's mix of rules.

label: החומא: the wall or rampart
note: The word is read the same way; the open question is whether it is the wall of the city or of the Temple enclosure. The research files place the entry at the east wall beside the East Gate (best-supported, medium).

label: בשן הסלע: the spur of the rock

readings.meaning: a rocky projection under the east rampart

note: Milik's preliminary reading differed, but his DJD commentary speaks of a rocky projection, as the text shown does. The phrase 'spur of the rock' occurs in the Bible only at 1 Sam 14:4, and the lexicon rates its meaning high.

label: כדין: bars or pitchers
note: Puech reads bet ('bars'), Lefkovits kaf ('pitchers'); the same split recurs at VII 10 and IX 3. It changes the kind of silver deposit, not the place; the text shown has Lefkovits's כדין, and the files do not choose.

label: שש: six
note: Milik's preliminary publication gave 'six hundred' here. The files record it only as an early reading, and the text shown has שש, 'six'.

label: ביאתו: its entrance

readings.meaning: the entrance, or the cache itself, lies under the great threshold

note: In the Mishnah the word means 'entering', never an architectural entrance, so the lexicon rates 'entrance' as medium. Puech leaves open whether the entrance or the cache itself lies under the threshold.

label: שבמזרח כחלת: east of Koḥlit

readings.meaning: a pool east of Tell es-Sultan (hypothesis)

note: Koḥlit is unplaced (see I 9). On Puech's Tell es-Sultan hypothesis this is a pool east of the tell; a stone reservoir at the spring there is reported but undated, so the files keep the entry at possible, low.

label: אמות {ב}ארבע: four cubits

readings.meaning: a repeated 'cubits' cancelled as a dittography
II 14 listed among disputed uses of 'cubit'

note: The files note a cancelled, repeated אמות in this entry and list II 14 among the disputed uses of 'cubit', but say it does not affect the location. The text shown instead cancels a ב before ארבע.

label: בחצר ◦◦◦: the court of …
note: The name of the court is lost and every edition restores it differently. The text shown restores the last letter of 'court' and leaves three letters unread; the files leave the name open and place entries 12 and 12a only as possibly in the Temple area.

label: תחת הפנא האחרת: the other corner

readings.meaning: one item with III 1–4; 'the scholars' split it

note: All agree this is a second corner of the same court; the question is whether it is a separate hiding place, which the files leave open. It matters because the Greek letters ΤΡ close this part.

label: ΤΡ: Greek letters

readings.meaning: perhaps terumah; gap of about 6 letters

note: Whether a third letter follows is disputed, and the files say only photographs could settle it (Q27). The group stands where the editors disagree about the division, and the ten-to-one numeral reading is one of the rules the files reject.

label: בשית: in the pit
note: The word is not in the Bible in this sense, and the Mishnah has it mostly as שיח, so the lexicon rates 'pit' as medium. The files record no editor who reads it differently here.

label: שבמלחמ: the Millo or the Esplanade

readings.meaning: the Esplanade: retaining walls and fill of the Temple platform

note: If the word is the Temple Esplanade, entries 13 and 14 lie in Jerusalem; if it means salt or a place Melaḥ, the setting is open, and the lexicon rates the meaning low. The files quote the word as שבמלה or שבמלח; the form shown here ends in an extra מ.

label: לבושין: garments
note: Wolters takes the 'my' as a sign that a high official wrote the list; Patrich objected that no writer marks his own list items as 'mine' (p. 296). The text shown has Puech's letters without his added ו.

label: ביאתא: its entrance
note: As at II 12, the lexicon rates 'entrance' as medium because Mishnaic usage means 'entering', not a doorway. The files record no editor who reads it differently here.

label: בקבר שבמלחמ: the tomb in the Millo

readings.meaning: by the Temple Esplanade; his site list names Alexander Jannaeus's tomb

note: This is the same disputed word as in III 8. A tomb by the Temple platform is known only from texts, so the files keep entries 13 and 14 as possible, low.

label: תחת המ ת: under the slab, or the body

readings.meaning: 'under the stone (of the ossuary)': a slab over a bone pit

note: The text shown reads המת, 'the dead', like Milik's early reading and Lefkovits; Milik's DJD text and Puech read a slab (מדף). The lexicon rates 'slab' low, because no Mishnah use of מדף is explicitly a tomb stone.

label: 13: the sum
note: The 13 shown here follows Milik and Lefkovits; Puech reads 14. The files give no preference.

label: שב כחלת: north(?) of Koḥlit
note: Both the name Koḥlit and the direction are Puech's restorations here; Milik saw only the letters …QH. The text shown restores the כ and marks other letters as damaged, so this mention of Koḥlit rests on Puech's reading, and the files treat the link as conditional.

label: 14: the sum

readings.meaning: a different figure (value not given in the files)

note: Part of the number is lost. Puech restores more signs in the lacuna before the preserved 14, and Lefkovits's figure differs; the text shown shows only 14.

label: ΣΚ: Greek letters

readings.meaning: the Ι cancelled, and engraved more deeply
first letter σ, χ or ξ, over another letter?

note: The first letter is disputed, and the files say only photographs could settle it (Q27). ΣΚ is the last Greek group: entries 16–20 follow on the same sheet without letters, and no tested hypothesis explains why they stop here.

label: באמא הבאה ◦◦: the conduit that goes to …
note: The goal of the conduit is lost, and no place name survives in this entry. Eshel says his Hyrcania restoration assumes a geographical order in the list, so the files keep Hyrcania and Tell es-Sultan only as possible, low.

label: בביאתך אמות ארבעין ואחת: as you enter, the distance
note: Only ארבע survives, so the figure is 14, 40 or 41 depending on the restoration; the text shown restores Milik's 41, in brackets. Whether a bare number after 'as you enter' is a depth or a distance is also disputed (Milik DJD C158/C160; Lefkovits p. 161).

label: שני הכיפין: the two cavities, trees or buildings

readings.meaning: 'the two tamarisks'; trees 'could easily have disappeared'

note: The landmark is read with kaf, bet or taw, and the הכיפין shown here matches none of the three forms reported. Caves of the period exist in the cliffs by Wadi Nuweiʿimeh, and the files test a cave pair (V/49 and a neighbour) only under Puech's reading; no source reports a pair of any kind.

label: שבעמק עכור: the Valley of Achor
note: The engraver wrote עכון; every edition takes it as Achor, and the text shown prints the corrected עכור. As at I 1, the choice between Wadi Nuweiʿimeh and the Buqeia is open, though the research files rate Wadi Nuweiʿimeh best-supported (medium) for this entry.

label: בשית האדמא: the earth pit

readings.meaning: 'earth pit': dug in ground, not rock

note: האדמא can mean 'earth' or 'red'. Red marl is common in the area (Puech 2015 p. 52 n. 206), so both senses fit the terrain in kind; no pit is reported.

label: שבשולי: at the edge or outlet

readings.meaning: the outlet of a spring (ʿEin Nebi Musa)

note: Milik's sense ties the entry to a spring; Puech's is only a position at the edge of the place. The files give no preference.

label: העצ לא: ʿAṣla, or 'the wood'

readings.meaning: Wadi el-ʿAṣla, part of the Mukellik–ʿAṣla–Daber torrent
one word; between ʿAyn Nabi Musa and the cliffs north of Qumran

note: Milik and Puech read one word carried over the line end, a place name known only in modern Arabic; Lefkovits reads two words and no place. The files keep ʿAṣla as possible, and which stretch of wadi is meant stays open (Q23), since Clermont-Ganneau describes a separate little Wady el-ʿAsala (SWP III p. 200).

label: בשית המזרחית: the eastern pit
note: 'The eastern pit' implies more than one pit. No pits are reported north of Tell es-Sultan, the files' working candidate for Koḥlit.

label: שבצפון כח לת: north of Koḥlit
note: Allegro's reading removes the place name; Puech and Milik keep Koḥlit. This entry and entry 60 are both 'north of Koḥlit' and could be one area, but Koḥlit itself is unplaced (see I 9).

label: ביגר: the cairn or the dam

readings.meaning: cairn; rejects 'dam': a flood 'could carry it away'
the dam where the Qumran aqueduct starts

note: The letters are secure; the meaning decides whether one looks for a burial cairn or a dam. Both kinds of feature existed at Qumran, but the dam is only reconstructed and would not settle the word, so the files leave it open.

label: גי הסככא: the valley of Sekakah

readings.meaning: 'Sekaka' = the whole Wadi Qumran; the biblical village = Kh. es-Samra
the lower valley, by the cultivated edge of ʿEin Feshkha

note: Both editors put the valley around Qumran, and the research files rate Wadi Qumran below Kh. Qumran best-supported (medium). No ancient name survives there, so the placement rests on the order of the entries and on 'from Jericho to Sekakah' (V 13).

label: ברוש אמת המים: head of the conduit

readings.meaning: the Qumran aqueduct, 'well preserved, even today'
the Wadi Qumran aqueduct, with a dam at its head
'the large channel carrying water to Sokokah/Qumran'
agrees: the aqueduct leading to Kh. Qumran

note: The letters agree, and the editors link this conduit with the Qumran aqueduct. The research files leave open which part is the 'head': the intake beside the basin (compared first), a branch junction, or a tunnel mouth downstream.

label: של גי ה: link to Sekakah
note: The word joining the conduit to Sekakah is lost: 'west of' puts the conduit on one side of Sekakah, while 'leading to' or 'at' fix no side, and the text shown restores של גי ה ('of the valley of'), which matches none of the restorations reported in the research files. The research files keep the models apart, note that Puech's choice itself assumes Qumran, and leave the question open.

label: סככא: which place is Sekakah

readings.meaning: the scroll's Sekaka = the whole of Wadi Qumran
biblical Sekakah = Kh. es-Samra in the Buqeia; the scroll's Sekaka = Wadi Qumran

note: Everyone reads Sekakah (Josh 15:61), and both main editors put entries 20–23 around Qumran, but Puech makes it the settlement and Milik the wadi. No ancient name survives there, so every Qumran placement stays conditional on this identification.

label: מן הצפון: from the north

readings.meaning: the water comes from the north (flow direction)
on the north side of the feature

note: The letters are secure, but 'from the north' may give the direction the conduit comes from or the side on which the cache lies. The research files test the two senses separately and leave the question open.

label: האבן הגדולא: the great stone

readings.ref: via Puech 2015 p. 55; rejected by Puech

note: Only 'great' (הגדולא) survives; 'stone' is a restoration, as the brackets in the text shown mark. The research files warn against choosing a boulder on the ground and then using it to confirm the restored word.

label: שלוש: depth of three
note: The depth figure is restored, and the text shown also restores most of it, in brackets. The research files do not choose among the restorations.

label: אשיח שלומו: Solomon's reservoir

readings.meaning: a Qumran reservoir excavated by de Vaux; 'undoubtedly' the cistern SE of the site
a legendary name, given a generation or more after 68 CE
legendary association of Secacah's water installations
records the parallel with Solomon's Pool in Jerusalem
reservoir (Milik's אשיח is a spelling variant)

note: The letters agree (the אשיח shown here is Milik's spelling of Puech's אשוח), but no source names any Qumran reservoir as Solomon's. The research files leave open which basin is meant and whether the name implies a late date (Q37).

label: שלומו: Solomon or Shallum

readings.meaning: 'Canal of Solomon': the site's main distribution channel

note: With Solomon, this trench pairs with the reservoir of entry 22; with Shallum, that link falls away. The research files ask for an independent review of the letter division and leave the question open (Q41).

label: הרגם הגדול: the great landmark

readings.meaning: a mound or a burial heap

note: The text shown has הרגם (final mem) where Puech reads הרגב (bet), and the landmark may be a boulder or a mound; the lexicon rates the meaning low. The research files say the reading must be settled before the 60-cubit distance can be used.

label: שבנחל הכפא: the Kippa ravine

readings.meaning: Wadi Kuteif; a stepped underground chamber there, 'probablement un tombeau'
follows Milik: Wadi Kuteif, between Jericho and Qumran

note: The letters agree, but the meaning of Kippa (rock or cavern) is disputed, and Wadi Kuteif rests mainly on the route (low confidence). The only chamber recorded there is undated and is not shown to be the tomb.

label: בביאה מירחו לסככא: from Jericho
note: Allegro's reading removes Jericho and the route; all later editors read 'as one comes from Jericho to Sekakah'. The research files treat this as a general approach to test, not a continuous route from entry 23.

label: הרגם: boulder or mound
note: The text shown has הרגם (final mem) where Puech reads הרגב, the same word as in entry 23. The lexicon rates its meaning low, so the landmark could be a boulder or a mound, and the files do not decide.

label: במשכן המלכא: the queen's building

readings.meaning: (same letters; no editor's gloss in the files)
a tomb or mausoleum, or a dwelling or enclosure

note: The letters are secure, but the building (tomb or dwelling) and the queen are not identified; the lexicon rates 'the queen' medium, and Josephus's queen references all concern Helena of Adiabene, whose monuments stood north of Jerusalem. The research files keep the Jericho area and the Tombs of the Kings as possible places only.

label: ביגר: cairn or dam

readings.meaning: a heap of stones that can hide a burial; 'tumulus'
possibly a dam (he says he does not understand the description)

note: A cairn is a heap of stones by a path; a dam is a water work, and Puech finds it 'difficult to imagine a ford and a dam side by side'. The research files follow the cairn reading, but no cairn is reported at any ford.

label: שבמגזת הכוהן הגדול: the High Priest's ford

readings.meaning: ford, at the Jordan ('doit être cherché au Jourdain')
'certainly denoting a ford (not a bridge, as Allegro thinks) over the Jordan'

note: A ford puts the cache at a river crossing, a bridge at a built structure. The research files place the entry at a lower Jordan ford near Jericho, with low confidence and no archaeology for any ford.

label: 22: the sum

readings.meaning: only the final 22 is read; the rest is lost

note: The 22 shown here matches Milik; Puech restores a larger total and Lefkovits reads no figure. The files record the difference without choosing.

label: קי◦ …: the damaged name

readings.meaning: Qi[dron] or Cy[pros]: Hyrcania's southern aqueduct

note: The broken word after 'conduit of' decides the place: Puech judges Kidron too long for the space and Kypros 'ruled out' (2015 p. 64 n. 252), and Eshel notes that column VIII spells קדרון without yod (p. 105 n. 31). The lexicon rates Puech's 'collection' low, and the place stays open.

label: האשיח הצפוני הגדול: the northern reservoir

readings.meaning: one of the pools of Hyrcania

note: Jericho is not preserved in this entry; it exists only in Puech's restoration, and the text shown fills that gap differently ('the great northern'). The research files keep the Jericho palaces, ʿAin Duk, Tell es-Sultan and Hyrcania as possible places only.

label: המקרא: cool room or vicinity

readings.meaning: the cool room (mem 'assured', whole 'probable rather than sure')
a 'cool room' would fit Jericho's bath installations

note: With Puech's reading the cave is next to a bath-house cool room; with Milik's it is only near the house of Haqqoz. The letters shown here are close to Puech's; the lexicon rates the meaning low and the files do not choose.

label: בית הקץ: house of Haqqoz

readings.meaning: house of the priestly family Haqqoṣ, placed at Tell el-Qos
the Haqqoṣ family; a Jericho property 'very probable'; abandons 'summer'

note: A family name points to a priestly estate; 'summer house' names only a kind of building. Phase 5 lowered Tell el-Qos to weak (a heap of stones), and the Jericho oasis stays possible only.

label: כדין: bars or pitchers
note: The first letter changes the silver from bars to pitchers, and the text shown has Lefkovits's כדין. The files record the difference without choosing.

label: בדוק: Doq

readings.meaning: the Hasmonean fortress Dok on the summit of Jebel Qarantal, NW of Jericho
the fortress on Ras Qarantal = Doq/Dagon
Doq, north-west of Jericho (the spring area)
'north-east of Jericho' (a slip, per the files)

note: The name is secure (1 Macc 16:15) and survives at ʿAin Duk, so Doq passes the name test. The files leave open whether the scroll means the summit fortress (Milik), the spring (Puech) or Kh. Abu Lahm (SWP) (Q24).

label: פנת … המזרחית: the eastern corner

readings.meaning: the eastern corner of the drying room
the eastern corner of the guard post
a corner of the eastern guard post

note: 'Eastern' can describe the corner or the building; with 'drying room' it describes the corner. The files say the reading must be settled before a building is chosen.

label: המשמרה: the landmark

readings.meaning: drying room; ṭet and ḥet 'indisputable', hmšmrh 'not likely'

note: The text shown follows Milik and Lefkovits; a fortress fits the Hasmonean fort reported on the summit, while nothing like a drying floor is reported. The files do not let the archaeology choose the reading, so the question is open (Q24).

label: פי יציאת המים: mouth of the outlet

readings.meaning: the head (start) of one of the Qelt aqueducts
a spring head, or a channel exit or junction

note: The letters agree, but the lexicon rates the phrase medium. The research files compare three Wadi Qelt features (ʿAin Qelt, the Jisr ed-Deir junction, the wall opposite Deir el-Kelt) and have not identified the outlet.

label: הכוזבא: Koziba or Buz

readings.meaning: Choziba: the Qelt gorge from ʿAin el-Qelt to Roman Jericho
probably the eastern part of Wadi el-Qelt

note: Most editors read Koziba, as does the text shown; Lefkovits reads Buz, and the drawings differ. Koziba gives the Wadi Qelt placement (medium), but the name is attested only from the 5th-century monastery.

label: הטור: wall, parapet or rock
note: The second landmark is a built wall for Milik, a parapet or mountain for Puech and a rock for Eshel. If it means a mountain, the research files note that the retaining-wall test no longer helps; the question is open.

label: 80: the silver sum
note: The 80 shown here follows Puech, while Milik and Lefkovits read 60. Lefkovits reports that the three drawings (Baker, Milik, Allegro) disagree here and that Milik's shows 60.

label: באמא: in the conduit
note: The first letters of the landmark are restored, as the brackets in the text shown mark. The research files list this among the restorations that affect the landmark; no other reading is reported.

label: בית אוצר: treasury or Bet Ḥaṣor
note: Puech reads a building, Milik a place name. The research files rate Milik's el-ʿAṣur / Baal-Hazor placement weak or ruled out because it rests on his emended text, and the entry stays at 'Jericho area, possible'.

label: אחור: Aḥiyah or Ḥazor
note: The אחור shown here matches neither form given in the research files. The lexicon rates the word low (Ahijah is a personal name in the Bible, never a place), and the question is open.

label: וספרין אסר: the last phrase

readings.meaning: and my scrolls, and a bar of silv[er]

note: The research files call this phrase uncertain, and the אסר shown here with the numeral 10 matches none of the reported readings. Wolters took the 'my' suffixes to point to a high official as author (p. 293); Patrich objected (p. 296).

label: בתך דר◦: inscription or steep slope

readings.meaning: the steep part of a slope

note: The landmark is either a written marker or a feature of the terrain; the letters shown here are not the כתב חרת of Puech and Lefkovits, and the files do not print Milik's Hebrew. The lexicon rates the meaning low, and the valley itself is not identified.

label: ביגר: cairn or dam

readings.meaning: a heap of stones that can hide a burial, beside a road or path
the dam where Hyrcania's southern aqueduct began

note: A cairn marks a path; a dam would tie the entry to Hyrcania's aqueduct. The research files follow the cairn sense for the Kidron placement, but no cairn is reported there.

label: פי צוק: mouth of the gorge

readings.meaning: gorge; reached shortly before Mar Saba
gorge 'a short distance before it reaches Mar Saba on the way from Jerusalem'

note: A gorge and a peak are different landmarks. Even with 'gorge', the Kidron is also a canyon where it leaves the escarpment, so the files leave the exact stretch open (Q34).

label: קדרון: Kidron or pottery
note: Wolters and Pixner remove the place name; the text shown reads קדרון without the article. The research files accept the Kidron placement (medium).

label: 7: the sum
note: The 7 shown here follows Puech and Lefkovits. Lefkovits reports that the drawings give 2, 4 or 7.

label: בשלף: fallow land

readings.meaning: fallow land, the counterpart of the irrigated land of entry 37
the uncultivated west slope of a ravine
upper fallow / lower irrigated: 'the most meaningful interpretation'

note: All the main editions read שלף, but Lefkovits allows a place name, and the lexicon rates the meaning medium. The files cannot test 'fallow land' on the ground.

label: השוא: the Valley of Shaveh

readings.meaning: Valley of Shaveh = King's Valley towards Beth ha-Kerem, not Bethso
ha-Šoʾ = Josephus's Bethso, the necropolis SW of Jerusalem (Baqʿah)
King's Valley = valley of Beth-ha-Kerem, used for the Kidron

note: The editors put the valley in different places: Puech towards Beth ha-Kerem, Milik in the south-west necropolis. The research files leave the valley unresolved (Q22) and rate the placement low.

label: 65: the sum
note: The 65 shown here matches none of the editions reported in the research files. Lefkovits reports that the drawings also disagree here.

label: בדור: irrigated land

readings.meaning: the low irrigated part of the Shaveh

note: The בדור shown here matches Beyer's letters, not Milik's or Puech's, and the lexicon rates 'irrigated land' low-medium. The research files note that only the Kidron–Hinnom candidate has a reported water source for irrigation.

label: בצויח בצריח: chamber or cippus
note: The engraved word is בצויח, and the text shown gives both the engraved and the corrected form. A chamber and a boundary stone are different landmarks, and the files do not choose.

label: בשובך: dovecote

readings.meaning: dovecote cut into the rock at the spring
a regular opening of a cave or rock face

note: The letters agree, but the kind of feature differs; most editors read dovecote (Puech 2015 p. 76 n. 318). No dovecote or rock opening is reported at the spring.

label: שבשולי הנטף: edge of ha-Naṭoph

readings.meaning: ʿAin en-Natuf in Wadi Khareitun, near the cave of St Chariton
the point where the spring emerges
a Galilee option for the place

note: The letters agree (Puech notes the waws are engraved like reš, CSS p. 72), and the research files follow ʿAin en-Naṭuf at medium confidence. The lexicon rates the name medium to high and records Lefkovits's Galilee option.

label: {שתין} חפור{ר}: two holes

readings.meaning: two holes or pits in the rock

note: For Milik this is a depth; for Puech it is two holes with no depth. The text shown marks שתין as cancelled, so it shows neither reading clearly, and the files do not choose.

label: ככרין: bars or pitchers
note: The research files report a בדין/כדין difference at IX 3, but the text shown has ככרין (talents), which matches neither. The files do not choose between bars and pitchers.

label: בחבלת השניא: the second terrace
note: Puech reads a common noun, Milik a place name found only in his text; the letters shown here follow Puech. The lexicon rates 'terrace' low-medium, and the files place the entry only in the Tekoa–Herodium area (possible).

label: 23 ף: twenty-three and a half

readings.meaning: the ½ sign may be 1 or 2 (left open)

note: Puech and Milik read the last sign (shaped like ף) as ½, and the text shown keeps it. The files leave the question open (Q8).

label: בצריחי החורון: Horites or Horon
note: The החורון shown here follows Milik's printed text, but his own drawing shows החורין with yod, as Puech reads. Beth-Horon depends on Milik's letters and on 'facing the Sea'; the lexicon rates the name low and the place is open.

label: בצריח: chamber or side

readings.meaning: in the chamber (ṣade inserted in his text)

note: Milik's drawing agrees with Puech's letters (ברוח); only Milik's printed text, which the display follows, has 'chamber'. The research files give this observation low weight until Puech's plates are checked.

label: הצופא ים: facing west or south
note: The direction decides between Upper Beth-Horon (Milik) and other places, and the text shown has ים. Milik's drawing shows only two signs, which somewhat favours ים, but the files keep the question open until Puech's plates are checked (Q14).

label: בזרב: channel or gutter
note: The word occurs in neither the Bible nor the Mishnah, and the lexicon rates its meaning low. No editor's gloss is given in the research files.

label: בקומעה: hole, or a place name
note: The research follows the reading 'hole', rates its meaning low and leaves entry 41 unmapped; Milik's place name Qobʿeh rests on an emendation and is rated weak or ruled out. Editors also split on the entry itself: Luria joins this line to entry 42, Beyer to entry 40, and Lefkovits allows 41 and 42 as one (Lef. pp. 293–296).

label: כסף מנה חרמ: the silver's description
note: Both editions have silver here, but the Phase 1 comparison counts the whole line as read differently. The files do not say which word carries Puech's 'much', so the exact point of difference is open.

label: בקול המים: waterfall or dam

readings.meaning: a waterfall; or, reading qyl, a dam or reservoir

note: What landmark these words name is uncertain: the research lexicon rates the meaning low. Puech allows a waterfall or a dam, and Høgenhaven reads IX 7–13 as a landscape marked only by natural features.

label: לכפת ביב: bend of the conduit

readings.meaning: by the bend of a built water conduit

note: Milik reads a village name where Puech reads common nouns; the research rates Kephar Nebo weak or ruled out because it exists only in Milik's emended text. The text shown has Puech's letters, לכפת ביב.

label: מזרח: east, or distance
note: For Milik this word gives a direction, for Puech a distance. The text shown follows Milik's letters (מזרח), not Puech's (מרחב).

label: שיבצפון פי הצוק: north of the gorge

readings.meaning: no 'north of' before the gorge's entrance
au nord de l'entrée de la gorge (north of the gorge's entrance)

note: Milik's 1960 translation lacked 'north of'; he added it in DJD III (1962), so the pit lies north of the gorge's mouth. The research lexicon rates צוק 'gorge' medium.

label: בית תמר: Beth Tamar

readings.meaning: objects that there is no gorge near Gibeah

note: The name is secure in the text but its site is not: the research lists Tell el-Ful (Gibeah) and Puech's Tekoa–Herodium area only as possible. No Beth Tamar has been located.

label: ביצ{ה}יאת גי פלע: the stony ground
note: Puech and Lefkovits agree on the letters but not on the sense; the research lexicon rates צחיאה medium-high and גר פלע, perhaps a place name, low. The text shown differs in letters: ביצ{ה}יאת and גי where Puech has בצחיאת and גר.

label: בשובך: dovecote or opening

readings.meaning: an opening (as he reads שובך in entry 38)

note: Most editors, Puech among them, read a dovecote; the Phase 5 review notes the same split as in entry 38, where Milik reads a cave opening or inspection hole. The research lexicon rates 'dovecote' medium-high.

label: שבמצד נאב בתחום: the fort's name
note: Puech reads a 'small fort' as one word, Lefkovits the Fort of Nobah, and Milik Masada with an aqueduct, which the research rates weak or ruled out because it depends on an emendation or a misplaced fragment. The text shown divides the letters as שבמצד נאב.

label: בעליאה השנית: the second level

readings.meaning: a structure of at least two levels

note: Milik changed 'second storey' (1960) to 'second ascent' (1962). The research lexicon rates עליה 'upper room, storey' medium.

label: בבור גר: plastered cistern
note: Puech and Lefkovits read the same letters but the sense is obscure; Milik reads another word, a wheel-well, and his DJD word list puts no cistern at X 3. The text shown has Puech's letters, בבור גר.

label: מזקות שרוו: its channels

readings.meaning: letters agreed with Lefkovits; sense obscure

note: מזקא/מזקות is a rare technical word found in neither the Bible nor the Mishnah, and the research lexicon rates its meaning medium. Phase 1 gives Puech's second word as שרוי where the text shown has שרוו.

label: באשיח שיבית הכרם: Beth ha-Kerem's reservoir

readings.meaning: a large built reservoir, not a household cistern
Ramat Raḥel, after Aharoni, who used the scroll's order

note: All editions read the name and the reservoir word the same way; the dispute is the site. The research keeps Ramat Raḥel but lowered it to low, because its known pools lie under fill with pottery as late as the 2nd century BCE and the identification partly rests on the scroll's own order.

label: בבואך לסמולו חפור: as you enter, left

readings.meaning: the cubits that follow give a distance
the cubits that follow give a depth

note: 'As you enter, on the left' is relative to the reservoir's entrance, not a compass bearing, and the text does not say from where one enters. Lefkovits and Milik apply different rules to the cubits that follow; the question is open (Q19).

label: אמות עסר: ten cubits, or feet

readings.meaning: cubits (printed corrected; the drawings have גמות)

note: Milik's 'feet' is otherwise unattested as a unit in Hebrew (Puech p. 198 n. 380), and his own drawing shows a gimel-shaped sign that others take as a miswritten alef; the research leaves the unit open (Q15). The figure is ten in Puech and in Milik 1962, twelve only in Milik 1960.

label: בים: basin or pool
note: Here ים is taken as a basin or pool, not 'sea' or 'west' as at IX 7; the research lexicon rates this sense medium. Milik reads the same word again at X 15.

label: גי זרד: the valley's name

readings.meaning: valley of Job, south-east of Jerusalem
for an original איב: the Vale of Job = Bîr Ayyûb

note: The name decides the setting: Puech and Milik's Addenda read a 'valley of Job' near Jerusalem, Lefkovits a 'Pure Valley', Wolters Zered. The text shown prints Wolters's letters גי זרד; the research rates the name low to medium and lists Bîr Ayyûb only as possible.

label: בצדו המערבי: west side, or spring
note: Milik and Lefkovits give a direction here; Puech reads an underground chamber by a spring, so his entry has no direction at this point. The text shown follows Milik (בצדו המערבי).

label: כפורין עסרין: twenty or ten cups
note: The facsimile drawings themselves disagree here, showing 10 or 20 (Baker, Milik, Allegro, as reported by Lefkovits). The text shown has עסרין, twenty, the figure in Puech's column of the Phase 1 table.

label: יד אבשלום: Absalom's monument

readings.meaning: the Hand of Absalom, in the SW necropolis (Baqʿah)
south-east of the city, in the Kidron below Siloam

note: All editions read the name; the dispute is which side of Jerusalem the monument stood on (Q18). The research places it in the Kidron at low confidence, on the order of the entries, and notes that the standing Kidron monument was first labelled Zacharias, not Absalom.

label: אמות: cubits, or feet

readings.meaning: cubits (printed corrected; the drawings have גמות)

note: The same problem as at X 6: Milik reads 'feet' where the others read 'cubits', while the figure, twelve, is agreed. The research leaves the unit open (Q15).

label: בים בית חמים: baths, or water outlet

readings.meaning: 'outlet', as used of the Gihon in 2 Chr 32:30

note: The kind of installation changes with the reading: an outlet or spring (Puech), baths (Milik) or a water closet (Lefkovits). The text shown has Milik's letters בים בית חמים, not Puech's יציאת המים.

label: של רחיל: Siloam, Rachel, or Jehu

readings.meaning: of Siloam (engraved ר read as ו, של restored)

note: Siloam is the research's best-supported place for this entry, but only at medium confidence and on condition that the engraved ר is read as ו (Q35). The text shown prints ר here (של רחיל).

label: השקות: the trough

readings.meaning: trough; confirmed on the pre-cutting photograph
a trough or gutter, with the cache under it

note: All editions read a trough or gutter here, and the research lexicon rates the meaning medium-high. A trough of the period has not been established at Siloam, so the feature itself stays unverified.

label: בברכא העליונה ב: pool, or Zadok's court

readings.meaning: its pool = the pool of Siloam (Birket el-Ḥamrâ)

note: Puech names Zadok already on this line (the only place where the name rests on his reading alone), Lefkovits restores an inner court, and Milik's Addenda restore the pool of Siloam. The files do not give Puech's letters here, so which words of the text shown his reading replaces is not stated.

label: ארבעת מקצועות: the four corners

readings.meaning: an inner corner (פנה: an outer one)
joins entries 49 and 50 as one unit

note: Lefkovits counts four deposits here, one at each corner, while Beyer joins entries 49 and 50 into one unit. Milik's Addenda return to the form 'their corners'.

label: זהב: gold, or none
note: Puech's text has gold in this deposit and Lefkovits's does not. The text shown has זהב, as Puech.

label: האסטאן: stoa, or ossuary
note: With 'stoa' the deposit lies below a corner of a Temple portico; with 'ossuary' the entry has no outside landmark. The research lexicon rates 'stoa' medium and places the entry, at medium confidence, on the Kidron slope below the south-east corner.

label: בקבר צדוק: Zadok's tomb

readings.meaning: tomb of Zadok, west bank of the Kidron below the SE corner
a monumental tomb with vestibule and court, near Siloam

note: The tomb itself is not identified; the research places the entry only at slope level and leaves open which bank of the Kidron. The research lexicon rates the name Zadok medium.

label: בהכסה: scarp, family plot, or ruin
note: Each reading gives a different kind of landmark, and the research lexicon rates the meaning low. The letters shown here הכסה match none of them exactly.

label: גנת צדוק: Zadok's court or garden

readings.meaning: across the torrent from the tomb of Zadok
the hoard lies at the top of a rock opposite the monument

note: The biblical and Mishnaic uses of גנה are 'garden', none of them funerary, so the research lexicon rates the meaning medium. The research places the entry on the Kidron's east slope at low confidence, since Zadok's court itself is not located.

label: המסמא הגדולא: the great slab
note: The research lexicon rates 'slab' high (m. Kelim 1:3). Only on Lefkovits's reading, which the lexicon calls rejected, is this a spiral staircase.

label: שבשוליה זהב חרם {בק}: base, channel, or sum

readings.meaning: at its base, it is consecrated; cancelled letters, no sum

note: Whether this deposit has a stated sum depends on the reading (Q9). The text shown, like Puech, has the cancelled letters {בק} and no numeral.

label: הסכין: colonnades, or knife

readings.meaning: compared with הסובב, the ledge of the altar

note: On one reading the tomb lies under the Temple galleries, on the other a rock called 'the knife' marks it; the research lexicon rates the meaning low. The text shown has הסכין with kaf, not סבין.

label: בני העמ: whose tomb

readings.meaning: the sons of … (a partly read name)

note: The reading decides whose tomb this is: the common people (Puech), a family named Obed (Lefkovits), or a family whose name Milik reads only in part. The research lexicon rates the phrase low.

label: טהור הו בו: of Jericho, or 'pure'

readings.meaning: my pure things are in it

note: This is one of only two lines where Jericho is preserved in Puech's text; Wolters, reading from the metal, found 'my pure things are in it' instead. The text shown has טהור here and no ירחו.

label: בבית אאשוחין: two reservoirs, or Bethesda

readings.meaning: rejects Bethesda; the site 'not completely certain'

note: Only Milik's emendation gives the name Bethesda, but the other reading still describes a double pool; the research keeps the Bethesda pools as best-supported (medium) while noting a second twin pool nearby. The text shown has אאשוחין, not Milik's אשדתין.

label: לימינ{מ}ית: the smallest basin?

readings.meaning: its smallest basin, which one can enter
the smallest basin (at Bethesda, the northern one)

note: Milik's and Puech's word for the smallest basin fits a twin pool with a smaller basin; Lefkovits reads a basin and a measure instead. The text shown has לימינ{מ}ית, which matches none of these readings.

label: במבא: entrance, or alley
note: In the Bible the word mostly means 'entrance'; every Mishnah example is מבוי 'alley', the sense Lefkovits takes. The research lexicon rates the meaning medium.

label: רובד: course or terrace (restored)

readings.meaning: pavement, terrace; restored on this line

note: The research lexicon marks this word as restored at XI 16 and rates its meaning medium. The text shown restores it too, in brackets.

label: בית המשכב: the burial chamber?
note: The phrase בית משכב does not occur in the Bible, and only a few uses of משכב are funerary. The research lexicon rates the meaning low to medium.

label: טיף: platform?
note: The word is not attested in this sense in the Bible or the Mishnah. The research lexicon rates 'platform' low.

label: מ: the cave (restored)
note: Only the מ survives; Puech restores 'cave', and his printed text and commentary spell the restoration differently. The files report no other editor's reading of this spot.

label: ככרין ששין: Milik's new item

readings.meaning: three items; this sum opens his item 59

note: Milik, followed by Pixner, Wolters, García Martínez, Vermes and Wise, splits entry 56 into three deposits and moves ככרין ששין and בידן into the following item; Puech and Lefkovits keep one entry. Separate deposits could lie at separate spots (Q6).

label: ביאתו מן המערב: entrance from the west
note: The direction changes with the reading. The text shown has מן המערב, as Puech; the research lexicon rates ביאה 'entrance' medium.

label: כוזין: juglets
note: Wolters says the original in Amman and two published facsimiles support כוזין. The text shown has כוזין, not Milik's בידן.

label: הבור: cistern, or burial niche
note: The landmark changes from a tomb feature to a water installation. The text shown has Milik's הבור; the research lexicon rates כוך medium.

label: בהר גריזין: Mount Gerizim
note: The name Mount Gerizim is not in doubt; the research lexicon rates it high. The findings log notes that the scroll's letters are גויזין, while Lefkovits, like the text shown, prints גריזין.

label: המעל{ה}א: the step
note: The engraved המעלה is corrected to המעלא, which the text shown marks with {ה}. The main editions read a step; only Allegro's 'entrance', which Puech rejects, differs.

label: השיח העליונא: the upper pit

readings.meaning: the upper pit ('upper' implies another pit)

note: The pit word differs between editions, but the kind of feature, a pit or shaft, does not. The text shown has השיח, Allegro's letters; the research lexicon rates Puech's שוחה low.

label: בית שם: Beth Sham or Beth Shean

readings.meaning: Beth Shean with final mem; or Beth Shem(esh), 'House of the Name', an unknown Beth Shem

note: Every other source spells Beth Shean with nun, so the scroll's final mem is the problem (Q16). The research keeps Beth Shean as best-supported (medium), noting that springs are common in that valley.

label: בביבא הגדולא: the great conduit
note: The word is agreed apart from a reading bkwkʾ that Puech rejects, and the research lexicon rates ביב 'conduit, drain' medium-high. No source consulted reports such a conduit at Kh. Ibziq.

label: הבור: Bezek, or another name

readings.meaning: ha-Bezek = Kh. Ibziq, 'for lack of anything better'
ha-Baruk: Banî Naʿîm and Hebron; in the Addenda, Hebron

note: Only the Bezek reading gives a place the research can test, Kh. Ibziq, which it rates possible; Milik's reading points to Hebron. The text shown has הבור, the letters of Wilmot and Wise, not Puech's הבזך.

label: מלבית הבור: house of Bezek, or tomb

readings.meaning: 'the house of Bezek' or 'the burial chamber'

note: The second instance may read bzk or kwk, so this is either a building named for Bezek or a burial chamber near the conduit. The text shown again has הבור.

label: שב{צח}צפון: situated, Smooth Rock, or Janoah

readings.meaning: situated; rejects Janoah on the engraving
the tunnel in the Smooth Rock

note: Only the Janoah reading would add a second place name beside Koḥlit; Puech rejects it and the research leaves it open (Q12). The text shown shows Milik's צח as cancelled letters, leaving שבצפון.

label: כחלת: Koḥlit

readings.meaning: Tell es-Sultan (old Jericho), as a hypothesis
Tell es-Sultan, north of Hasmonaean and Herodian Jericho
Tell es-Sultan, if Achor is Wadi Nuweiʿimeh

note: The name is secure, but no ancient source outside the scroll places it, and the research records eleven or twelve proposals. It rates Tell es-Sultan only possible (low); Milik's Carmel, Goranson's Transjordan and Zissu's Samarian desert break the order of the entries.
